name: Nile
hook: The river that made Egypt, from Lake Victoria to the Aswan High Dam.

facts.label: 4,160 miles
facts.statement: The Nile runs about 4,160 miles from Burundi to the Mediterranean and was once said to rise in the Mountains of the Moon.

facts.label: Lake Victoria
facts.statement: Lake Victoria, bordered by Uganda, Tanzania and Kenya, is the Nile's chief reservoir and was identified by John Speke in 1858.

facts.label: Khartoum
facts.statement: The Blue Nile and the White Nile meet at Khartoum, Sudan's capital, to form the main Nile.

facts.label: Cairo
facts.statement: Cairo, Egypt's capital, lines the Nile's eastern bank; Herodotus called Egypt "the gift of the Nile."

facts.label: the Aswan High Dam
facts.statement: The Aswan High Dam, begun in 1960, created Lake Nasser, one of the world's largest artificial lakes.

facts.label: papyrus
facts.statement: Papyrus, the plant used to make ancient writing material, grew in the Nile delta.

facts.label: the Battle of the Nile
facts.statement: At the 1798 Battle of the Nile, Admiral Nelson destroyed the French fleet, a victory that made him a baron.
